result.topic_en: Gauss tabulates indices (discrete logarithms) of residues modulo 61 with primitive root 2, groups them into biquadratic classes, and uses 4x4 schemes in unknowns β, γ, m to derive the decomposition of a prime p = 4m+1 into two squares, checked with 61 = 25 + 36.

methods.what: Table of powers of the primitive root 2 modulo 61 (index table)
Representation of a prime p=4m+1 as a sum of two squares in terms of cyclotomic parameters
Quadratic relation between γ, β, m obtained by summing squared class-counts
Expression of class-number products (cyclotomic numbers) as linear combinations over the four biquadratic classes
